problem: Calculate the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola ${x}^{2}+2x-2y-1=0.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Vertex of a Parabola by Completing the Square

feedback.problem: Calculate the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola ${x}^{2}-6x-2y+19=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard equation of an upward- or downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ is

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

where $p$ is constant.

To write the given equation in this form, we need to group the $x$-terms on the left-hand side and complete the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-6x-2y+19 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-6x & =2y-19 \\ (x-3)^{2}-9 & =2y-19 \\ (x-3)^{2} & =2y-19+9 \\ (x-3)^{2} & =2y-10 \\ (x-3)^{2} & =2(y-5) \\ (x-3)^{2} & =4(\frac{1}{2})(y-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex are $(h,k)=(3,5).$
